SUBJECT:       AGENDA ITEM #7, PLACER COUNTY LOCAL AGENCY FORMATION
               COMMISSION CALL FOR NOMINATIONS – ALTERNATE SPECIAL
               DISTRICT REPRESENTATIVE


Background

The Placer County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) has opened the nomination
period for an open alternate Special District representative seat to fill the remainder of the term,
which will run through May 2028. The presiding officer (Board Chair/President) of each
independent special district may nominate any director currently serving on an independent
special district board within Placer County.

Nominations must be submitted to Placer County LAFCO by 4:00 p.m. on Tuesday, November
2, 2026.

Upon the closing of the nomination period, LAFCO will review all nominations for
completeness and eligibility. If only one valid nomination is received, that nominee will be
deemed appointed. If more than one nomination is received, a mail-ballot election will be
conducted.

Recommendation

The Board to discuss whether they would like to nominate any director currently serving on an
independent special district board within Placer County as an alternate Special District
representative to serve on the Placer County Local Agency Formation Commission, if they so
choose.

Election of Special District Representative to Placer LAFCo Call for Nominations: Special
District Member

Nomination Guidelines and Requirements:

1.        Authorized Signature: The nomination form must be signed by the district’s
          presiding officer, or the presiding officer’s alternate as designated by the
          governing body. While a formal board action to nominate a candidate is not
          required under the statute, the signature of the presiding officer or alternate is
          mandatory.
2.        Designation of Alternate: If an alternate has been designated by the governing
          body, please include a copy of the official meeting minutes or minute order
          documenting this designation.
3.        Statement of Qualifications: Each nomination may submit a one-page
          "Statement of Qualifications" for the nominee. This statement will be distributed to
          all districts during the voting period.
4.        Submission Deadline: The nomination period begins on Tuesday, September
          29, 2026, and will close on Tuesday, November 2, 2026, at 4:00 PM.

Next Steps: Once the nomination period concludes, LAFCo staff will review all
nominations for completeness and eligibility. If only one valid nomination is received,
that nominee will be deemed appointed. If more than one nomination is received, a
mail-ballot election will be conducted. A ballot package—including the statements of
qualifications and voting instructions—will be emailed to all 36 independent special
districts.

Please submit the completed nomination form and the one-page statement of
qualifications via email to lafco@placer.ca.gov no later than 4:00 PM on Tuesday,
November 2, 2026.

Thank you for your commitment to ensuring that independent special districts remain
effectively represented on the Commission. Should you have any questions, please
contact our office at (530) 889-4097.

SUBJECT:       AGENDA ITEM #8, CONSIDER RESOLUTION 16-2026 IN
               APPRECIATION OF CAPTAIN JAMYE STOWELL


Background

The attached Resolution 16-2026 in Appreciation of Captain Jamye Stowell recognizes the
valuable service and contributions of Jamye Stowell to the North Tahoe Fire Protection District
during her 24 years of service.

This Resolution provides the Board of Directors with the opportunity to formally recognize
Jamye Stowell’s years of dedicated service and express the District's sincere appreciation and
best wishes for her future endeavors.

Recommendation

Adopt Resolution 16-2026 in Appreciation of Captain Jamye Stowell.

RESOLUTION 16-2026

                  A RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE
                       NORTH TAHOE FIRE PROTECTION DISTRICT
                     IN APPRECIATION OF CAPTAIN JAMYE STOWELL


WHEREAS, the Board of Directors of the North Tahoe Fire Protection District are aware of the years of
valuable and dedicated service provided by Captain Jamye Stowell; and

WHEREAS, Jamye began her career with the North Tahoe Fire Protection District in November 1998 as
a part-time firefighter and became a full-time firefighter in December 2000; and

WHEREAS, Jamye was promoted to Engineer in December 2001 and Captain in June 2019,
demonstrating her dedication, leadership, and commitment to the District and the community; and

WHEREAS, Jamye retired from the District on December 16, 2022, leaving behind a legacy of service,
leadership, and commitment that has made a lasting impact on the North Tahoe Fire Protection District
and the communities it serves; and

WHEREAS, throughout her career, Jamye received several notable recognitions, including Firefighter of
the Year in 2006 and a Field Save Award in 2008, reflecting her professionalism and outstanding service;
and

WHEREAS, throughout her career, Jamye has demonstrated unwavering dedication, courage, and
professionalism, earning the respect and appreciation of her colleagues and making lasting contributions
to the North Tahoe Fire Protection District and the communities it serves; and

WHEREAS, while Jamye's retirement marks the closure of an outstanding career in public service, the
friendships she has built, the knowledge she has shared, and the example she has set will continue to
benefit the District for years to come; and

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that by this Resolution, the Board of Directors intends to
recognize the twenty-four (24) years of service provided by Captain Jamye Stowell and to extend its
thanks and grateful appreciation for her selfless and dedicated service.

PASSED AND ADOPTED this 27th day of October 2026 by the Board of Directors of the North Tahoe
Fire Protection District, Placer County, State of California, by the following roll call vote:

SUBJECT:       AGENDA ITEM #9, CONSIDER RESOLUTION 17-2026 IN
               APPRECIATION OF BATTALION CHIEF SARAH LAGANO


Background

The attached Resolution 17-2026 in Appreciation of Battalion Chief Sarah Lagano recognizes
the valuable service and contributions of Sarah Lagano to the North Tahoe Fire Protection
District during her 19 years of service.

This Resolution provides the Board of Directors with the opportunity to formally recognize
Sarah Lagano’s years of dedicated service and express the District's sincere appreciation and best
wishes for her future endeavors.

Recommendation

Adopt Resolution 17-2026 in Appreciation of Battalion Chief Sarah Lagano.

RESOLUTION 17-2026

                  A RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE
                       NORTH TAHOE FIRE PROTECTION DISTRICT
                 IN APPRECIATION OF BATTALION CHIEF SARAH LAGANO

WHEREAS, the Board of Directors of the North Tahoe Fire Protection District are aware of the years of
valuable and dedicated service provided by Battalion Chief Sarah Lagano; and

WHEREAS, Sarah began her career with the North Tahoe Fire Protection District in June 2005 as a part-
time firefighter and became a full-time firefighter in July 2007; and

WHEREAS, Sarah was promoted to Engineer in July 2013, Captain in 2017, and Battalion Chief in
January 2021, demonstrating her dedication, leadership, and commitment to the District and the
community; and

WHEREAS, Sarah retired from the District on March 16, 2024, leaving behind a legacy of service,
leadership, and commitment that has made a lasting impact on the North Tahoe Fire Protection District
and the communities it serves; and

WHEREAS, throughout her career, Sarah received several notable recognitions, including Firefighter of
the Year in 2010 and two Field Save Awards in 2009 and 2013, reflecting her professionalism and
outstanding service; and

WHEREAS, Sarah played a critical role in the District’s physical fitness program and assisted in the
design of the workout room at Station 51. She was an integral part of implementing several involved IT
projects such as the District iPads, First Due, and IT security. Sarah also helped establish the Regional
Rescue Team with our mutual aid partners; and

WHEREAS, over the course of her service, Sarah has demonstrated exceptional leadership, sound
judgment, and a steadfast commitment to excellence while serving in progressively responsible
assignments, and fostering a culture of honor, integrity, and professionalism; and
WHEREAS, while Sarah's retirement marks the closure of an outstanding career in public service, the
friendships she has built, the knowledge she has shared, and the example she has set will continue to
benefit the District for years to come; and

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that by this Resolution, the Board of Directors intends to
recognize the nineteen (19) years of service provided by Battalion Chief Sarah Lagano and to extend its
thanks and grateful appreciation for her selfless and dedicated service.

PASSED AND ADOPTED this 27th day of October 2026 by the Board of Directors of the North Tahoe
Fire Protection District, Placer County, State of California, by the following roll call vote:

SUBJECT:       AGENDA ITEM #11, CONSIDER RESOLUTION 19-2026 AUTHORIZING
               THE FIRE CHIEF, OR HIS DESIGNEE, TO ENTER INTO THE AGENCY
               FUNDING AGREEMENT FROM THE TRUCKEE-TAHOE AIRPORT
               DISTRICT TO FULLY FUND THE RIVER ROAD PROJECT 0, FUELS
               REDUCTION PROJECT IN THE AMOUNT OF $400,000


Background

After successful implementation of the hand thinning component for River Road Project 1, and
utilization of extension funding to support North Tahoe Fire’s Community Day and Fire Adapted
Communities in Alpine Meadows, North Tahoe Fire is now eligible to accept additional funding
to support River Road Project 0. The Tahoe-Truckee Airport District (TTAD) continues to
support regional fuels reduction projects, and a new funding agreement for $400,000 is available
to reduce fuels on 10 acres of shovel ready land owned by the US Forest Service (USFS) along
the Hwy 89 corridor between Tahoe City and Alpine Meadows Road.

The US Forest Service has a National Environmental Protection Act (NEPA) Decision Memo in
place covering the entire River Road corridor as part of the larger Lake Tahoe West Project
footprint. This covers the removal of hazard trees and the reduction of wildfire risk using various
fuels management tactics. This project will be known as River Road Project 0 and has a 21-
month period of performance. This project will directly support ingress/egress along the Hwy 89
Corridor in locations deemed to be of the highest priority based on the computer modeling used
in the 2025 Community Wildfire Protection Plan. The project would further support the
partnership between NTFPD and TTAD, which has proven to be a tremendous asset since 2024.
The project would also allow for a stronger partnership between NTFPD, the USFS Lake Tahoe
Basin Management Unit (LTBMU) who owns the land, the Tahoe City Public Utilities District
(TCPUD) who manages the bike path, and Cal-Trans who manages the highway and the
easement where we will be working. An ability to further utilize TTAD funding to reduce fuels
where it is most beneficial to support ingress/egress, safety, and community assets would be
tremendously advantageous to the mission of NTFPD, and the residents and visitors we serve.
NTFPD has reviewed the Agency Funding Agreement and is seeking approval from the Fire
Board to enter into this agreement.

Recommendation

Adopt Resolution 19-026, authorizing the Fire Chief, or his designee, to enter into the Funding
Agreement Amendment from the TTAD in the amount of $400,000 to reduce fuels on 10.0 acres
of high-priority treatment areas near the Hwy 89 Corridor.

Background

Following the consolidation of Meeks Bay Fire Protection District into North Tahoe Fire
Protection District, the District became a multi-county agency and is now required to file its
Conflict of Interest Code with the Fair Political Practices Commission (FPPC).

As part of this process, the District has prepared a revised Conflict of Interest Code to reflect its
current organizational structure, designated positions, and disclosure categories. The revised
code has been prepared in coordination with the FPPC.

Recommendation

Adopt the revised North Tahoe Fire Protection District Conflict of Interest Code.

Conflict of Interest Code for the
                             North Tahoe Fire Protection District



    The Political Reform Act (Government Code Section 81000, et seq.) requires state and local
government agencies to adopt and promulgate conflict of interest codes. The Fair Political
Practices Commission has adopted a regulation (2 California Code of Regulations Section
18730) that contains the terms of a standard conflict of interest code, which can be incorporated
by reference in an agency’s code. After public notice and hearing, the standard code may be
amended by the Fair Political Practices Commission to conform to amendments in the Political
Reform Act. Therefore, the terms of 2 California Code of Regulations Section 18730 and any
amendments to it duly adopted by the Fair Political Practices Commission are hereby
incorporated by reference. This regulation and the attached Appendix, designating positions and
establishing disclosure categories, shall constitute the conflict of interest code of the North
Tahoe Fire Protection District (District).
    Individuals holding designated positions shall file their statements of economic interests
with the District, which will make the statements available for public inspection and
reproduction. (Gov. Code Sec. 81008.) The Board Members, Fire Chief/ District Treasurer, and
Director of Finance and Administration must file their statements of economic interests
electronically with the Fair Political Practices Commission. All other statements will be
retained by the District.
